title: MOSIP Overview
content:
# MOSIP Overview

MOSIP (Modular Open Source Identity Platform) is an open-source platform that helps governments build a robust foundational identity system. It is designed to be modular, so countries can use only the components they need.

## Key Features

- **Modular architecture** — each component (enrollment, authentication, resident services) is independently deployable.
- **Privacy by design** — biometric and demographic data is encrypted at rest and in transit.
- **Multi-language support** — supports 100+ languages via Unicode-compliant storage.
- **Open source** — published under MPL 2.0 license on GitHub.

## Core Modules

1. **Pre-registration** — residents submit demographic data and book enrollment appointments online.
2. **Registration** — biometric capture (fingerprints, iris, face) and demographic verification at enrollment centers.
3. **ID Authentication (IDA)** — real-time identity verification via OTP, biometric, or demographic match.
4. **Resident Services** — self-service portal for residents to update data, track requests, and download credentials.
5. **Partner Management** — onboard and manage authentication service providers (ASPs) and relying parties.

## Supported Biometrics

MOSIP supports fingerprint (slap and single), iris, and face biometrics using the ABIS (Automated Biometric Identification System) interface.

title: ID Authentication
content:
# ID Authentication (IDA)

The ID Authentication module is the core verification engine of MOSIP. It allows service providers to verify a resident's identity in real time.

## Authentication Types

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| OTP | One-time password sent to registered mobile/email |
| Biometric | Fingerprint, iris, or face match |
| Demographic | Name, date of birth, gender, or address match |
| Multi-factor | Combination of the above |

## API Flow

1. A relying party sends an authentication request with encrypted resident data.
2. IDA decrypts, validates, and matches against the registration database.
3. A signed response (`authStatus: true/false`) is returned within 2 seconds.

## Security

- All requests use RSA-2048 or ECC-P256 encryption.
- Session keys are wrapped with the partner's certificate.
- Response tokens use HMAC-SHA-256 for tamper detection.

## Integration

Partners integrate via the `/idauthentication/v1/auth/{partner-id}/{apikey}/{uin}` REST endpoint.
Use the partner SDK (Java/Python available) to handle key management and request signing automatically.

## Error Codes

- `IDA-MLC-007` — missing mandatory field
- `IDA-MLC-009` — invalid partner certificate
- `IDA-DEA-001` — biometric data hash mismatch
- `IDA-OTP-001` — OTP expired (valid for 3 minutes)

title: Registration Client
content:
# Registration Client

The Registration Client is a thick-client Java application installed on enrollment center machines. It captures biometrics and demographic data and uploads them to the registration processor.

## System Requirements

- OS: Windows 10 64-bit (Linux support planned)
- RAM: 16 GB minimum
- Storage: 500 GB SSD
- Biometric devices: SBI 2.0 compliant

## SBI (Secure Biometric Interface)

All biometric devices must implement the SBI 2.0 specification. The Registration Client discovers devices via the device discovery API on localhost port range 4501–4600.

## Packet Structure

Each enrollment creates an encrypted registration packet containing:
- Demographic data (JSON)
- Biometric data (ISO 19794 formats)
- Documents (PDF/JPEG)
- Audit trail

Packets are AES-256 encrypted and uploaded to the registration processor via a secure sync mechanism.

## Offline Mode

The Registration Client can operate offline for up to 30 days. Packets are queued locally and synced when connectivity is restored.

## Upgrade

Upgrades are pushed automatically via the software update service. Operators must not manually copy JAR files — always use the built-in update mechanism.

## Troubleshooting

- If biometric devices are not detected, restart the device service: `net stop mosip-device && net start mosip-device`.
- Packet upload failures are logged at `%APPDATA%\mosip\logs\registration.log`.

title: Deployment Guide
content:
# Deployment Guide

MOSIP 1.2.0 is deployed on Kubernetes using Helm charts. The reference deployment uses a 3-control-plane, 9-worker node cluster.

## Infrastructure

- Kubernetes: 1.26+
- Helm: 3.12+
- PostgreSQL: 14+ (for all databases)
- MinIO: RELEASE.2023-06-19 (object storage)
- Keycloak: 21+ (IAM)

## Helm Charts

All charts are published at `https://mosip.github.io/mosip-helm/`. To add the repository:

```bash
helm repo add mosip https://mosip.github.io/mosip-helm/
helm repo update
```

## Deployment Order

1. Deploy infrastructure: PostgreSQL, MinIO, Keycloak, Kafka
2. Deploy kernel services: Config server, Auth manager, ID generator
3. Deploy registration services: Registration processor, Registration manager
4. Deploy IDA: Auth server, OTP manager, Internal auth
5. Deploy resident services and admin portal

## Health Checks

All services expose `/actuator/health` endpoints. Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes use these automatically.

## Scaling

The registration processor is horizontally scalable — add worker nodes and increase the `replicaCount` in the Helm values. IDA can handle 1,000 authentications/second per pod.

## Production Checklist

- Enable HSM (Hardware Security Module) for key storage
- Configure external PostgreSQL with SSL
- Enable audit log shipping to SIEM
- Disable debug logging in all services

title: Partner Management
content:
# Partner Management

The Partner Management module allows the MOSIP admin to onboard organizations that will use MOSIP's authentication services.

## Partner Types

| Partner Type | Use Case |
|---|---|
| Authentication Partner (AP) | Verify resident identity via IDA |
| Credential Partner (CP) | Issue verifiable credentials |
| Device Provider | Supply SBI-compliant biometric devices |
| FTM Provider | Supply Foundational Trust Module chips |
| MISP | Manage trusted service providers |

## Onboarding Steps

1. Partner registers at the PMS portal with organization details.
2. Admin reviews and approves the partner application.
3. Partner uploads a CA-signed X.509 certificate.
4. Admin assigns policy groups (which data fields are shared).
5. Partner receives API key and begins integration.

## Policy Group

A policy group defines which authentication types and data attributes a partner is allowed to request. Example: a banking partner might be allowed biometric + OTP but not raw demographic fields.

## API Key Rotation

API keys are valid for 1 year. Partners must rotate keys before expiry:
```bash
curl -X POST https://{mosip-host}/partnermanagement/v1/partners/{partnerId}/apikey/rotate \
  -H 'Cookie: Authorization=<token>'
```

## Certificate Expiry Alerts

The system sends email alerts 30, 15, and 7 days before a partner certificate expires. Expired certificates cause authentication requests to fail with error `IDA-MLC-009`.
